news.title: England Women in World Cup 2027 play-offs: Lionesses have obligation to prove themselves after Spain disappointment
news.lede: When England were consigned to the World Cup play-offs back in June, it felt like a massive step backwards. How were the European champions not a shoo-in for the next major tournament in the international calendar? The Lionesses only missed out by a whisker, finishing their qualifying campaign with 15 points from a possible 18. But it's difficult to overlook how we got here.

news.title: From packs to pitches: How Lay’s RePlay became a global football movement
news.lede: In 2019, Lay's came up with a novel way of using old chip packets. That idea has since become a part of football's cultural landscape. It started with two ambitious football people, a piece of paper, and a question: Could Lay’s packaging be given a second life as a place to play football? In the middle of the COVID-19 pandemic, with the world, in effect, shut down, Adam Warner, then Senior Director of Global Sports Marketing at Lay’s, and a colleague began sketching out an idea that seemed ambitious, if not slightly insane.

news.title: Big test for Tillies stars as Montemurro begins World Cup auditions
news.lede: Joe Montemurro has nine months to work out how to keep the Matildas in the race for the World Cup. Australia’s upcoming friendly opponents will be the key for him to work out who is up for the challenge of taking on the world’s best. Football’s pinnacle tournament is set to be hosted in the sport’s spiritual home – Brazil – next year, with Australia wasting no time locking in three fierce competitors to get a taste of the talent that will go far in the tournament. Caitlin Foord and Sam Kerr are back in national team colours this week.

news.title: Wiegman praises Toone’s attitude after late Lionesses recall for Greece playoff
news.lede: Manchester United midfielder left out of initial squad. First leg of World Cup playoff is on Friday in Crete. Sarina Wiegman heaped praise on Ella Toone for her positive reaction to being left out of England’s initial squad for their Women’s World Cup playoff against Greece, after recalling the Manchester United midfielder for Friday’s first leg in Heraklion, Crete. An injury sustained by Lucy Bronze, described by Wiegman as “really small”, prompted the England right-back to return to Chelsea and Wiegman called up Toone, who travelled to Greece from Spain, where she had organised a training routine during the international window.

news.title: Greece vs England: How Ella Toone’s Lionesses snub could boost her World Cup chances
news.lede: Ella Toone may have started this international break on the outside looking in, but she looks set to emerge from it with her chances of making it to Brazil next summer strengthened. Toone was dropped for the World Cup play-off games against Greece after struggling for form at the start of the season with Manchester United. England head coach Sarina Wiegman admitted Toone's performances had not been up to the expected standard and laid down a challenge for the two-time Euros winner. news.title: Motsepe Lauds Moroccan Football, Urges Africa to Build on World Cup Gains
news.lede: Rabat - Confederation of African Football (CAF) President Patrice Motsepe has hailed Morocco’s football experience while calling on African countries to build on the progress made at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Motsepe made the remarks on Thursday during the opening of CAF’s strategic conference on Sal Island in Cape Verde. The CAF president said the performances of African teams at the 2026 World Cup showed that the continent’s ambitions have grown. He stressed that African football should no longer be satisfied with simply participating in major international tournaments.
